correctness.rationale: For 1<theta<2, the full-branch cusp map has inverse branches contracted by Lambda^{-1} with Lambda=1+theta/2. Assigning fair Bernoulli cylinder weights gives the unique maximal-entropy measure mu and its distribution-function tent conjugacy. Near the repelling endpoint 0, g0(u)=u/Lambda+O(u²), so repeated inverse iterates satisfy Lambda^n g0^n(delta)->positive finite constant; exact cylinder masses 2^-n imply mu([0,r])~_{two-sided} r^{d0} for d0=log2/logLambda. The right endpoint maps smoothly near 0, transferring d0. At the cusp f(c±r)=1-theta*r-2K sqrt(r), the exact two-branch mass identity sends its interval to [1-s(r),1] with s(r)≈sqrt(r), giving exponent dc=d0/2. Smooth noncritical inverse branches transfer dc to all dense finite preimages; since dc<1, H has +infinite derivative there, and endpoints with d0>1 give zero. Uniqueness of the W^{2,1} acim together with ergodicity and nonsingularity under f shows mu singular and H’=0 Lebesgue-a.e. Independent numerical inverse and exponent checks at theta=1.1,1.4,1.9 corroborate only boundary formulas.
